method: Full pinned C implementation read; Git blob and SHA256 verified. No new execution or conventional MetroHash vector comparison.
findings: State retains32-byte tail, four64-bit accumulators and use_sse flag; constructors zero state and use fixed initialization constants. State copy clones whole struct. Steal copies accumulators locally and processes tail without consuming live state.

All seeded one-shot128 wrappers feed four native-order seed bytes before message, including seed0. A direct fresh streaming state without that prefix therefore does not have identical input semantics. Conventional MetroHash compatibility is not implied by wrapper name.
256-bit mode concatenates outputs of variant1 and variant2 states. It has no separately defined256-bit compression and should not be treated as an independently verified algorithm.
METRO_FILL_XS narrows size_t length to int even for empty retained tail. Large direct updates can narrow or overflow signed byte-count arithmetic before memcpy; no large-update failure executed.

CRC functions are compiled under HAVE_MM_CRC32_U64 and mostly annotated target(sse4.2), while use_sse chooses scalar versus CRC behavior. Correct selection depends on caller CPU capability; passing TRUE alone does not detect CPU support.

Native-word input loads and memcpy output preserve host-dependent representation. The implementation has no total-length field; algorithm identity must be judged from actual implementation rather than assumed upstream MetroHash semantics.
limits: No streaming runtime parity, CRC target qualification or performance measurement.
